column3: “Jesus” and “the people” make subjects explicit; the passive hearing becomes active.
The coming and bringing become passive; “men” is supplied.
“Jesus” supplies the pronoun; lowering the mat becomes lowering the man on it.
“Son” specifies child; the historical present becomes past.
“Levi” makes the final subject explicit; the historical present becomes past.
“Levi’s” identifies the house; the historical present becomes past.
“Often” is supplied; the question is reordered around the disciples’ not fasting.
“Guests of the bridegroom” interprets sons of the bridal chamber.
“Time” replaces days; the final “on that day” is not expressed.
The final elliptical phrase becomes a passive statement.
“Jesus” makes the subject explicit; the historical present becomes past.
